rute-03-mara.context: Naomi left Bethlehem in a time of famine, with her husband and two sons. In Moab, all three died. Now she returns with only her daughter-in-law Ruth, and the women of the town barely recognize her.
rute-03-mara.focusQuestion: What name would you give your hardest season, and would you say it before God?
rute-03-mara.keywordGloss: The name Naomi asks for herself: it means bitter, which is how she feels coming back empty.
facts: When they arrived in Bethlehem, the women asked whether this was Naomi.
Naomi asked them to call her Mara, not Naomi.
She said the Almighty had made her life very bitter.
Naomi left full, but the Lord brought her back empty.
She felt the Lord had turned against her.
Naomi and Ruth arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

rute-04-asas.context: Ruth was gleaning in Boaz's field when he arrived and asked about her. On learning she was the Moabite who had returned with Naomi, Boaz protected her; now she wants to understand such favor.
rute-04-asas.focusQuestion: In what area of your life do you need to place yourself under God's care?
rute-04-asas.keywordGloss: An image of God's care: like a bird covering its young, he shelters those who seek refuge in him.
facts: Ruth bowed down and asked why she was favored, being a foreigner.
Boaz had heard all that Ruth did for her mother-in-law after her husband died.
Ruth left her father, her mother, and her homeland to come to an unknown people.
Boaz asked the Lord to repay what Ruth had done.
Ruth sought refuge under the wings of the God of Israel.
Boaz ordered that Ruth be allowed to glean even among the sheaves, without being rebuked.

rute-05-capa.context: Naomi told Ruth to go to the threshing floor where Boaz, their relative, would spend the night guarding the harvest. Ruth did everything her mother-in-law said and, in the middle of the night, spoke with him alone.
rute-05-capa.focusQuestion: What do you need to ask for boldly, trusting the character of the one who can help?
rute-05-capa.keywordGloss: Spreading one's cloak over someone is asking for covering and commitment: here, redemption by the close relative.
facts: Ruth went to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law told her.
She came near, uncovered Boaz's feet, and lay down.
Ruth asked Boaz to spread his cloak over her, because he is the redeemer.
Boaz said her last kindness was greater than the first.
The whole town knew that Ruth is a woman of noble character.
There was another redeemer closer than Boaz.

rute-lealdade-01-rute-e-noemi.context: Naomi was widowed in Moab, also lost her two sons, and decided to return to Bethlehem. She tries to send her Moabite daughters-in-law away so they can rebuild their lives; Orpah goes back, but Ruth stays.
rute-lealdade-01-rute-e-noemi.focusQuestion: Whom would you not abandon, even with no guarantee for the future?
rute-lealdade-01-rute-e-noemi.keywordGloss: Ruth does not just go along with Naomi: she binds herself to her, to her people, and to her God.
facts: Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
Naomi said Ruth's sister-in-law had gone back to her people and her gods.
Ruth declared that Naomi's people would be her people and Naomi's God her God.
Ruth said she would die and be buried where Naomi died.
Seeing that Ruth was determined to go with her, Naomi stopped urging her.
The two arrived in Bethlehem, and the whole town was stirred because of them.

rute-lealdade-02-nos-campos-de-boaz.context: Ruth, the Moabite widow who came with Naomi to Bethlehem, went out to glean leftover grain in a field. The field belonged to Boaz, a relative of Naomi's late husband, and he noticed her among the workers.
rute-lealdade-02-nos-campos-de-boaz.focusQuestion: Where has God already placed protection and provision on your path without your noticing?
rute-lealdade-02-nos-campos-de-boaz.keywordGloss: Boaz does not send Ruth away: he places her with his female workers, under his protection.
facts: Boaz told Ruth not to glean in another field.
Boaz told Ruth to stay close to his female workers.
Boaz ordered the young men not to touch Ruth.
Ruth could drink from the water the young men drew whenever she was thirsty.
Ruth had come to Bethlehem with Naomi.

rute-redencao-01-o-resgatador.context: Boaz redeemed the family at the town gate and married Ruth. A son was born, and the women who once heard Naomi's lament now celebrate with her in Bethlehem.
rute-redencao-01-o-resgatador.focusQuestion: What ending can God write in a story you once called bitter?
rute-redencao-01-o-resgatador.keywordGloss: The one who redeems what was lost: the women see in the birth the redeemer God gave Naomi.
facts: The women said the Lord had not left Naomi without a redeemer.
They wished that the boy's name would become famous in Israel.
The neighbor women named the boy Obed.
Obed is the father of Jesse, and Jesse is the father of David.
The genealogy begins with Perez and passes through Hezron.
Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.

rute-redencao-02-desafio-linhagem.context: This challenge reviews the ending: Boaz redeemed the family, Ruth had a son, and the women of Bethlehem celebrated with Naomi. The final genealogy shows where this small story will lead.
rute-redencao-02-desafio-linhagem.focusQuestion: What part of your story, small today, can God connect to something greater?
rute-redencao-02-desafio-linhagem.keywordGloss: The line of generations linking the boy from Bethlehem, Obed, to King David and, centuries later, to Jesus.
facts: The women said the Lord had not left Naomi without a redeemer.
The neighbor women named the boy Obed.
Obed is the father of Jesse, and Jesse is the father of David.
The genealogy begins with Perez and passes through Hezron.
Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.
The list ends with Jesse fathering David.
